response.text:
The rejection came from putting both voided journals' reversals into one group with corrects_jrnl_no=2461, which made the group unbalanced for the 2461 group. The fix is to submit a separate, self-balanced correction for each voided journal. I can only make one call, so I'll submit the correction for the first voided copy (JRNL 2461, INV 802), which is balanced on its own, and note the second copy as still needed.

Key checks: the original 2461 lines are DR 5300 19556.55 / CR 2000 19556.55, so the reversal is DR 2000 19556.55 / CR 5300 19556.55, in open period 11. Each journal balances. Voiding INV 802 is the only status change, and it is permitted because this is a duplicate_invoice finding and INV 802 is the open copy (INV 28 is paid and is kept).

Note: the invoice 801 / JRNL 2460 reversal (DR 2000 / CR 5100 1245.08) must be submitted as a separate correction with corrects_jrnl_no=2460, along with the 801 void. I'm not able to submit it in this same call.

arguments.reasoning: F001 duplicate invoice, pair V0024 65026-28. INV 28 (paid, JRNL 1045) is kept. INV 802 (open, JRNL 2461, a duplicate of the same invoice and amount) is voided. This correction fully reverses the only two lines of JRNL 2461 (DR 5300 / CR 2000 19556.55) with a self-balancing journal in open period 11, and it is referenced to 2461 alone so the group nets to zero. The prior attempt mixed the reversal of JRNL 2460 into this group, which unbalanced it; that is now handled separately. The matching correction for the other duplicate (INV 801, JRNL 2460, V0010 94645-557, DR 2000 / CR 5100 1245.08, period 11, void INV 801) must be submitted as its own correction referencing 2460. Payments link only via APPAYM; the open duplicate should have no payment rows, and this should be confirmed before the void is applied.
